rem:hydrogen-orbitals:
Remark Hydrogen orbitals: the electron word around the Borromean anchor. The picture.

Hydrogen couples an electron to a small Borromean proton. The proton occupies the center as a compact \mathcal{B}_3 formed of three unknots with \mathrm{Vol} \approx 7.328. The electron is the word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 (electron knot), whose closure is the Hopf link. It loops around the proton and Hopf-links to it.

\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=4em, column sep=5em]
  & \underset{\text{\normalsize electron } e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0}{\bigcirc\!\!\!\bigcirc}
    \ar[d, "\oplus"', "\text{Hopf}", dashed] & \\
  & \underset{\text{\normalsize small } \mathcal{B}_3}{\bullet}
    & \\
  & \underset{\text{proton (anchor)}}{\mathrm{Vol} \approx 7.328} &
\end{tikzcd}

The Borromean volume pins the massive proton in place. The Hopf link has no hyperbolic volume. The electron mass m_e is the CAL-1 input, not derived here. The Hopf link \oplus provides the electromagnetic binding.

Shell transitions as strand-adding curls.

The ground state is e_1 = e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0, with writhe w = 3. Photon absorption is the strand-adding curl: it appends the next generator,

  e_n = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\,\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_n \in B_{n+2}
  \;\longmapsto\;
  e_{n+1} = e_n\,\sigma_{n+1} \in B_{n+3}.

Appending \sigma_{n+1} is a Markov stabilisation, so the closure stays the Hopf link. The word stays Gröbner–Shirshov reduced, and the level shows as its length. Each curl raises the writhe by 1:

  n \to n + 1
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  w \to w + 1,
  \qquad\text{so}\qquad
  n = w - 2 = 1, 2, 3, \ldots
  \quad\text{for}\quad w = 3, 4, 5, \ldots

This is item 1 of the shell--writhe correspondence. Where the added curls sit in the brane tower is not re-derived for the ruled electron.

Backup reading. If the electron is the trefoil \sigma_0^3 \in B_2, a level step adds two Reidemeister I curls on the same strand, w \to w + 2, and n = (w - 1)/2. That reading puts the ground state (w = 3) in the base space \mathcal{S}_0 and the extra curls of w = 5 in the blow-up \mathcal{S}_1. The sub-shell count below is also built on it.

Sub-shells from resonance modes (backup reading).

This count has not been re-derived for the ruled electron. Its closure has two components, and no counterpart of the trefoil normal-bundle construction below is on record for it.

The embedded backup trefoil T_{2,3} vibrates transversely within its normal bundle N_{T_{2,3}} in the Bring surface. Laplacian eigenvalues on the trefoil curve govern the resonance frequencies. The mode integers \ell = 0, 1, 2, \ldots label the standing-wave patterns:

  • Mode \ell = 0: Uniform (no oscillation) — the s orbital.
  • Mode \ell = 1: One wavelength around the curve — the p orbital.
  • Mode \ell = 2: Two wavelengths — the d orbital.

At linking level n, the Seifert surface has effective length proportional to n. Only modes with wavelength \geq L/n fit. This yields the cutoff \ell = 0, 1, \ldots, n - 1. Each mode \ell vibrates transversely in ambient 3-space. Projected onto the sphere, the 2\ell + 1 standing-wave orientations match the spherical harmonics Y_\ell^m. Thus:

  \sum_{\ell=0}^{n-1} (2\ell + 1) =  n^2
  \quad\text{orbitals per shell.}

This sum reproduces the observed capacity for all n.

Note on geometric counting.

The sum \sum(2\ell + 1) = n^2 matches standard quantum mechanics. The backup trefoil model identifies \ell with trefoil resonance modes and n with the writhe framing number. The remaining step requires a proof:

The space of sections of the normal bundle N_{T_{2,3}} of the trefoil in the Bring's surface, at total framing twist k = 2(n-1), has dimension n^2.

This is stated as The orbital space at shell n is the space of framing-k sections of the normal bundle in the Bring's-surface chapter.

The two ingredients of the count have different sources, and only one of them is representation-theoretic. The 2\ell + 1 orientations are the dimension of the irreducible \mathrm{SO}(3) representation V_\ell carried by the mode, matching the spherical harmonics Y_\ell^m. The cutoff \ell \leq n - 1 is not: it is the length-and-framing bound already used above, that only modes of wavelength at least L/n fit along the Seifert surface. In the eigenvalue form \lambda_\ell \leq \lambda_{n-1} this is an arithmetic consequence rather than a group-theoretic one, and it is proved with no symmetry group entering the argument.

sec:topological-mass-formula-transcenden:
Through the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, the topological mass formula expresses particle mass ratios in terms of hyperbolic volumes \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) of link complements. By the Borel–Zagier theorem, hyperbolic volumes are periods of mixed Tate motives evaluated through the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z) at algebraic shape parameters z \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}} and are expected to be transcendental over \mathbb{Q}.

This section compiles the master knot-formula table across the particle spectrum, proves Chern–Simons evaluation faithfulness and its corollaries, formulates the single-volume irrationality conjecture (the weaker companion of the hyperbolic-volume transcendence conjecture stated with the topological mass formula), and establishes three-knot jet-order independence.
sec:hyperbolic-volumes-prose:
Hyperbolic volumes and the topological mass ansatz. Inertial mass originates in the topology of knot complements. The framework identifies every particle with a knot or link K (skein decomposition). Each knot carries a hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(K). This evaluates the volume of the complete hyperbolic metric on the complement S^3 \setminus K, computed via the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm. Torus knots, such as the trefoil 3_1, have zero hyperbolic volume. Hyperbolic knots have positive volume.

The framework identifies the Higgs boson with the figure-eight knot 4_1 (cohomological embedding). Its volume is

  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) = 6\,\Lambda(\pi/3)
    \approx 2.02988321281931,

where \mathrm{Cl}_2 denotes the Clausen function and \Lambda(\theta) = \mathrm{Cl}_2(2\theta)/2 the Lobachevsky function. The complement S^3 \setminus 4_1 decomposes into two regular ideal tetrahedra, each of volume \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) = 3\,\Lambda(\pi/3) \approx 1.01494.

The topological mass formula defines the mass \mathfrak{m}(K) of a particle with knot type K as

  \mathfrak{m}(K) =  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{2}},
  \qquad
  \hbar_q  :=  1 - q^{-1}.

Here q > 1 represents the aether parameter and \hbar_q represents the quantum planck constant. The mass functional \mathcal{M} is not additive for composite states. It satisfies a q-deformed Skein recursion at every crossing in the color-exchange diagram.

prop:cs-evaluation-faithfulness:
Proposition Faithfulness of the Chern--Simons evaluation on the brane tower. Let \Phi_n(K) denote the tower-level volume contribution from the tower decomposition. Let \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) denote the n-th quantum characteristic class.

The Chern--Simons evaluation map is faithful at each tower level. For every hyperbolic knot or link K in the Descartes spectrum,

  \kappa_n \neq 0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \Phi_n(K) \neq 0.

If \kappa_n defines a non-trivial obstruction in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}), the Chern--Simons period integral over the n-th twisted sector yields a non-zero real contribution to \mathrm{Vol}(K).
rem:cs-evaluation-faithfulness-corollari:
Remark Corollaries of Chern--Simons faithfulness and relation to Mostow rigidity. Corollaries.

  1. No accidental cancellation. The Peiffer identity in the crossed groupoid conjugates a^{(n)} by g^{(n)} but preserves the period. The \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)-adjoint action functions as an automorphism of the band \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}, not as a projection to zero.
  2. Infinite non-trivial contributions. The Yekutieli lifting theorem guarantees \kappa_n \neq 0 for all n. Faithfulness therefore implies the volume receives new data at every tower level.
  3. Path to algebraic independence. If each \Phi_n(K) carries arithmetically independent data, the series \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = \sum_n \Phi_n(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2) = \sum_n \Phi_n(5_2), and \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = \sum_n \Phi_n(\mathcal{B}_3) satisfy no polynomial relation. A finite polynomial cannot absorb infinitely many independent contributions.

Relation to Mostow rigidity. Mostow rigidity guarantees the total volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) defines a topological invariant. This proposition refines the invariant into a graded series \{\Phi_n(K)\}_{n \geq 0}, controlled by cohomological obstructions. Rigidity ensures convergence. Faithfulness ensures non-degeneracy at each grade.
conj:single-volume-irrationality:
Conjecture Irrationality of a single hyperbolic knot volume. Each of the three non-zero QOU hyperbolic volumes is irrational:

  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \notin \mathbb{Q},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Vol}(5_2) \notin \mathbb{Q},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \notin \mathbb{Q}.

Remark. This conjecture remains open. No hyperbolic 3-manifold volume has ever been proven irrational. The figure-eight volume 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) evaluates the Clausen function at a rational multiple of \pi. Its irrationality reduces to the irrationality of \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \sin(k\pi/3)/k^2. This represents a Dirichlet L-value at s = 2 for the character \chi_{-3}. This evaluation remains unknown.

Ap'ery (1978) proved \zeta(3) \notin \mathbb{Q}. The constant \zeta(3) equals one-quarter the hyperbolic volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron. Knot complement volumes sum Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm values D(z_i) at algebraic arguments. The arithmetic of these sums lies beyond current methods.

Irrationality forms the weakest link in the transcendence chain:

  \text{irrationality}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \mathbb{Q}\text{-linear independence (Borel--Zagier)}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \text{algebraic independence.}

Proving any of these statements for the QOU volumes demands a breakthrough in transcendental number theory.
conj:borel-zagier-qou-volumes:
Conjecture Rational linear independence of QOU hyperbolic volumes (Borel--Zagier). The three QOU hyperbolic volumes are \mathbb{Q}-linearly independent:

  a_1 \,\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) + a_2 \,\mathrm{Vol}(5_2)
  + a_3 \,\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 0,
  \quad a_i \in \mathbb{Q}
  \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
  a_1 = a_2 = a_3 = 0.

This represents a special case of the Borel--Zagier conjecture. The Borel--Zagier conjecture asserts the \mathbb{Q}-linear independence of volumes of pairwise non-commensurable hyperbolic 3-manifolds.

Non-commensurability

Two manifolds are commensurable if they share a finite-sheeted cover. The three QOU complements occupy distinct commensurability classes:

  • S^3 \setminus 4_1: The unique arithmetic hyperbolic knot complement. It is commensurable with \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathcal{O}_3).
  • S^3 \setminus 5_2: A non-arithmetic complement with a cubic trace field. This field breaks commensurability with 4_1.
  • S^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3: A 3-component link complement. Its cusp geometry is incompatible with the knot complements. The ratios \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)/\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 3.610 and \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)/\mathrm{Vol}(5_2) \approx 2.592 confirm the link volume is not a simple rational multiple of either knot volume.

K-theoretic formulation

The Borel regulator maps K_3(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \to \mathbb{R}. Volumes of hyperbolic 3-manifolds lie in its image. The conjecture equates to the statement that the Borel regulator acts injectively (modulo torsion) on the K_3-elements corresponding to these three complements.

Linear independence is strictly weaker than algebraic independence but strictly stronger than irrationality.
conj:three-knot-jet-order-independence:
Conjecture Jet-order algebraic independence (QOU-attackable reduction). For every truncation order N, the Habiro-ring expansions of the coloured-Jones invariants for the three QOU knots/links,

  J_{4_1}(q),\qquad J_{5_2}(q),\qquad J_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q)
  \;\in\; \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]},

are algebraically independent modulo (q;q)_{N+1} over \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}]. Equivalently, the Jacobian of their cyclotomic coefficient vectors \bigl(c_0(K), \dots, c_N(K)\bigr) for K \in \{4_1, 5_2, \mathcal{B}_3\} possesses full rank 3 for all N \ge N_0.

This statement supplies a computationally viable target. It implies the algebraic-independence conjecture provided the surreal-limit bridge holds. The ideal approach requires the full transcendence machinery (Grothendieck periods and the Borel regulator on K_3(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})), which remains out of reach. This reduction replaces that machinery with three framework-native tools and one remaining gap.

Finiteness and decidability. Each J_K(q) admits a canonical jet-order grading. The Habiro cyclotomic expansion J_K(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n(K)\,(q;q)_n organizes the invariant such that the n-th term forms the vertical jet-degree n component of the categorical generating function. This aligns with the body-order filtration grading the binding series G(x;q) = \sum_n B_n x^n. Algebraic independence to order N imposes a finite-rank condition on the truncated coefficient matrix. The claim is strictly decidable.

The three framework tools.

  1. Jet-order filtration supplies the grading. Independence is verified order-by-order. Reid (1991) anchors the base order. Because 4_1 is the unique arithmetic hyperbolic knot, its trace field \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) is rigidly distinct from the cubic trace field of 5_2 and the link field of \mathcal{B}_3 at order 0.
  2. Gröbner–Shirshov filtration certifies each order. The reduction engine computes the elimination ideal I_N = \bigl(\text{relations among } J_{4_1}, J_{5_2}, J_{\mathcal{B}_3} \bmod (q;q)_{N+1}\bigr) \subseteq \mathbb{Q}[q,q^{-1}][x,y,z]. Full Jacobian rank holds if and only if I_N carries no generator of total degree \le N. This translates "no polynomial relation" into a normal-form computation natively executed by the skein engine. The base-order certificate is proved and directly witnessed by computation. The h-jet expansion about q=1 of the canonical Markov traces \mathrm{tr}_M(K) for the three canonical braid words yields jet-Jacobian rows (\tfrac14, -1, \tfrac{55}{16}), (\tfrac12, 0, -\tfrac1{16}), and (1, 0, 0). Their elimination determinant is \tfrac1{16} \neq 0 (LU pivots (\tfrac14, 2, \tfrac18)). Full rank 3 holds unconditionally at the base order. This constitutes a finite determinant test on real data. Higher orders require no further computation. The order-N Jacobian contains this non-singular 3\times3 minor as a column-submatrix. Its rank is therefore \ge 3. The three rows strictly bound the rank by 3. The rank must be exactly 3 at every N, as rank is monotonically non-decreasing in the column count. The two endpoints of this argument are proved. The base minor is full-rank via explicit invertibility. The abstract monotonicity principle holds: any monotone, row-bounded rank function equal to 3 at the base order remains 3 for all N \ge 3. The column-extension linkage discharging the principle's hypotheses for the order-N Jacobian is supplied as a structural input. Per-order independence reduces to this structural linkage.
  3. Surreal error bounds supply the bridge to the limit. The correct geometric picture is parallel transport on the projective state fibre. The coloured-Jones invariant J_K(q) acts as the holonomy of the categorical connection, parallel-transported along the aether q-deformation path on \mathcal{S} = P \times_G \mathbb{CP}^1. The volume is its singular-limit asymptotics \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \tfrac{2\pi}{n}\log\lvert J_K(e^{2\pi i/n})\rvert. The surreal error bound measures the transport error as q deforms toward the root-of-unity point. This error is non-Archimedean because the target point is a singularity of the connection. The error is an infinitesimal in the surreal field. Three conditions must hold for the bridge:
    • (I1) Uniformity in jet order. The transport error must be bounded uniformly in N. The connection's curvature is uniformly controlled along the deformation path, independent of the truncation order. Any error growing with N severs the transfer.
    • (I2) Archimedean projection. The error inhabits the surreal fibre level, carrying the \mathrm{Im}(q) structure. The volume is archimedean (\mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0). The surreal infinitesimal must project to exactly 0 under \tau. A non-infinitesimal archimedean shadow would inject a spurious polynomial relation among the volumes.
    • (I3) Monodromy separation. Transport around the cusp is flat only at generic q. At the root-of-unity limit, the holonomy accumulates cusp/modular monodromy. The bound must isolate the physical holonomy, which yields \mathrm{Vol}, from this monodromy artifact. The framework's surreal-number error field provides the natural setting for this uniform bound. The reduction splits the previously monolithic hypothesis. Uniformity (I1) and the (I2)∘(I3) composition are proved. The two physical inputs remain conjectural: the physical-holonomy shadow vanishes (I2), and the monodromy shadow vanishes (I3). These are now isolated as precisely stated hypotheses.

The one remaining gap. This reduction does not prove the deep conjecture. It reduces the conjecture to a single native lemma:

Bridge lemma (open). If \{J_{4_1}, J_{5_2}, J_{\mathcal{B}_3}\} are jet-order independent for all N with a surreal-bounded uniform error, then \{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)\} are algebraically independent over \mathbb{Q}(q_0).

The reduction secures a strategic advantage. Remark Proof sketch: baryon product from alt. Proof sketch. By Schur–Weyl duality at level n = 3 in three dimensions (Schur–Weyl mass decomposition), the \mathrm{S}_3-module

  V \;:=\; \bigotimes_{k=1}^{3}\, T_{c_k}\mathbf{C}

decomposes into isotypic components labelled by partitions of 3:

  \;=\; \mathrm{Sym}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Alt}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Std}^{\oplus 2}.

  \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_3|} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{S}_3}

  \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} (c_i - c_j)^2

Proposition Aether-level bar T-duality: \mathcal{E}_q \leftrightarrow \mathcal{E}_{1/q}. The bar involution \iota \colon q \mapsto q^{-1} on the aether parameter line lifts to an aether-level T-duality between elliptic curves of the Descartes family (Descartes elliptic curve):

  \iota_*\,\mathcal{E}_q  =  \mathcal{E}_{q^{-1}}.

Here \iota_* is the pull-back of \iota along the aether parametrization q \mapsto \mathcal{E}_q. Under \iota_*:

  1. Discriminant locus: The pole \Delta(\mathcal{E}_q) = 0 at q = 1/\varphi^2 pairs with \Delta(\mathcal{E}_{1/q}) = 0 at q = \varphi^2 (skew-dual golden node).
  2. j-invariant: The rational involution j \mapsto j^*, induced by q \mapsto q^{-1} on the Weierstrass coefficients, relates j(\mathcal{E}_q) and j(\mathcal{E}_{1/q}).
  3. Confinement band: The curve \mathcal{E}_q is non-degenerate if and only if q \in \mathcal{B} (bar-self-dual band). The involution \iota fixes \mathcal{B} setwise.

Target-space T-duality (self-duality of the color curve) exchanges X \leftrightarrow z on the single curve \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{col}}. Bar T-duality instead acts on the moduli parameter q. These commuting dualities generate a \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2-action on the moduli stack of Descartes-family curves.
prf:bar-t-duality-aether:
Proof Proof of bar t duality aether. The substitution q \mapsto q^{-1} in the Weierstrass coefficients p(q) and r(q) yields rational functions p^*(q) = p(q^{-1}) and r^*(q) = r(q^{-1}), defining the curve \mathcal{E}_{q^{-1}} : y^2 = x^3 + p^*(q)\,x + r^*(q). The map \iota_* \colon \mathcal{E}_q \to \mathcal{E}_{q^{-1}} is defined by (x, y, q) \mapsto (x, y, q^{-1}) on the total space \mathcal{X} = \{(x, y, q) : y^2 = x^3 + p(q)x + r(q)\} and is an involution since \iota \circ \iota = \mathrm{id}.

(1) The condition \Delta(\mathcal{E}_q) = -4p(q)^3 - 27r(q)^2 = 0 at q = 1/\varphi^2 implies \Delta(\mathcal{E}_{1/q}) = -4p(1/q)^3 - 27r(1/q)^2 = 0 at 1/q = 1/\varphi^2, meaning q = \varphi^2.

(2) The j-invariant j(\mathcal{E}_q) = -1728 \cdot 64\,p(q)^3 / \Delta(q) pulls back along \iota to j^*(q) := j(\mathcal{E}_{1/q}) = j(q^{-1}), a well-defined rational function of q.

(3) By bar-self-dual confinement band, the open interval \mathcal{B} = (1/\varphi^2, \varphi^2) is the maximal \iota-invariant open subset of \mathbb{R}_{>0} avoiding the golden nodes. This makes it the maximal locus where both \mathcal{E}_q and \mathcal{E}_{1/q} are simultaneously non-degenerate. \square

This property implies that any statement of the form "\mathcal{E}_q has property P for q \in I \subset \mathcal{B}" automatically yields its bar conjugate: "\mathcal{E}_{1/q} has property P for q \in \iota(I)." Proofs extend about the elliptic family from the sub-classical wing (1/\varphi^2,\,1) to the super-classical wing (1,\,\varphi^2) by composing with \iota_*. Thus, a deconfinement statement such as "q < 1/\varphi^2 \Rightarrow deconfined" yields the bar companion "q > \varphi^2 \Rightarrow deconfined" directly.

Aether-level bar T-duality is the geometric shadow of the Iwahori–Hecke bar involution \overline{\,\cdot\,} \colon H_n(q) \to H_n(q^{-1}) given by \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. Because the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q arises from the Markov trace (Descartes elliptic curve), the Hecke bar involution descends to \iota on the moduli parameter.
prop:bar-apply-transfer:
Proposition Bar-transfer principle: one-sided bounds on bar-invariant properties extend for free. Let P \colon \mathbb{R}_{>0} \to \mathrm{Prop} be a bar-invariant property of the aether parameter:

  \forall\,q > 0,\quad P(q) \iff P(q^{-1}).

For every a > 0:

  1. Lower bound transfer. \bigl(\forall q > a,\; P(q)\bigr) \iff \bigl(\forall q < a^{-1},\, q > 0 \Rightarrow P(q)\bigr).

  2. Two-sided extension. If a < 1 and \bigl(\forall q \in (a, a^{-1}),\, P(q)\bigr), then \bigl(\forall q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} \setminus \{a, a^{-1}\},\, P(q)\bigr) does not follow in general. If P is continuous on \mathbb{R}_{>0}, bar-invariance forces P to extend symmetrically across both endpoints.

  3. Negation transfer. \bigl(\exists q < a,\, q > 0 \land \neg P(q)\bigr) \iff \bigl(\exists q > a^{-1},\, \neg P(q)\bigr).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at q_0. Categorical or q-deformation identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring. Only their archimedean realisation requires specialisation here.
prf:bar-apply-transfer:
Proof Proof of bar apply transfer. (1) Assume \forall q > a,\, P(q). Let q < a^{-1} with q > 0. Then q^{-1} > a, so P(q^{-1}) holds, which implies P(q) by bar-invariance. The reverse implication is dual. (3) Negate (1). (2) This is false in general. For example, P(q) = \mathbf{1}_{q \in (a, a^{-1})} is bar-invariant on (a, a^{-1}) but false outside. Under continuity, every limit point of \{q : P(q)\} is bar-conjugate to a limit point of \neg P, forcing the symmetric extension. \square

The bar-transfer principle establishes that a one-sided aether bound for a bar-invariant property yields the bar-conjugate bound. If one proves

  q_0 > 1/\varphi^2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{E}_{q_0}\text{ is non-degenerate}

then bar-applying yields

  q_0 < \varphi^2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{E}_{1/q_0}\text{ is non-degenerate}

The property holds on the super-classical wing (1, \varphi^2) exactly as established on the sub-classical wing (1/\varphi^2, 1). Both derivations fold into a single statement on the bar-self-dual band \mathcal{B} = (1/\varphi^2, \varphi^2).

Every two-sided stability statement of the form

  q \in (a, a^{-1}) \Longleftrightarrow \text{stable}

with a bar-invariant stability condition requires proving only one inequality. The companion inequality is automatic. Apply this to the following eligible bar-invariant predicates:

  • \Delta(\mathcal{E}_q) < 0 (single real component), via bar T-duality.
  • Slater-strict feasibility of the confinement SDP formulated \iota-equivariantly in q.
  • Markov-trace positivity on the Hecke algebra (\sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}).
  • j-invariant finiteness of the Descartes elliptic curve.
prop:golden-quartet-galois:
Proposition Golden quartet \{1/\varphi, -\varphi, \varphi, -1/\varphi\} as the root set of x^4 - 3x^2 + 1. The golden quartet

  Q  :=  \bigl\{\,1/\varphi,\;-\varphi,\;\varphi,\;-1/\varphi\,\bigr\}

is the complete root set of the quartic polynomial

  P(x)  :=  x^4 - 3x^2 + 1
   =  (x^2 - x - 1)(x^2 + x - 1)

over \mathbb{Q}, and \varphi \cdot (1/\varphi) = 1. Replacing \sqrt{5} by -\sqrt{5} in \varphi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2 gives -1/\varphi, and in 1/\varphi = (\sqrt{5}-1)/2 gives -\varphi.

The finer structure (the two Galois orbits Q_+ = \{\varphi, -1/\varphi\} and Q_- = \{1/\varphi, -\varphi\} of \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})/\mathbb{Q}), their exchange by the bar involution \iota \colon x \mapsto x^{-1}, and the transitive faithful action of \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})/\mathbb{Q}) \times \langle\iota\rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2 on Q) is argued in the proof but is not part of this formal statement.
prf:golden-quartet-galois:
Proof Proof of golden quartet galois. Direct expansion yields:

  (x^2 - x - 1)(x^2 + x - 1)
  = x^4 + x^3 - x^2 - x^3 - x^2 + x - x^2 - x + 1
  = x^4 - 3x^2 + 1.

The quadratic factors are the minimal polynomials over \mathbb{Q} of \varphi and 1/\varphi, respectively. Their roots form Q_+ and Q_-.

For \tau \in \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})/\mathbb{Q}) acting by \sqrt{5} \mapsto -\sqrt{5}:

  \tau(\varphi) = \tau\!\left(\tfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)
   =  \tfrac{1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}  =  -1/\varphi,
  \tau(1/\varphi) = \tau\!\left(\tfrac{-1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)
   =  \tfrac{-1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}  =  -\varphi.

Thus Q_+ and Q_- are the two Galois orbits.

The bar involution \iota maps \varphi \mapsto 1/\varphi \in Q_-. Since \varphi \cdot 1/\varphi = 1 and (-\varphi) \cdot (-1/\varphi) = 1, \iota exchanges Q_+ and Q_-.

The product action of G on Q generates the orbit G \cdot \varphi = Q:

Element of G Image of \varphi
(\mathrm{id}, \mathrm{id}) \varphi
(\tau, \mathrm{id}) -1/\varphi
(\mathrm{id}, \iota) 1/\varphi
(\tau, \iota) -\varphi

Since all four elements appear and |G| = 4 = |Q|, the action is transitive. \square

Eliminating \zeta_5 Galois arithmetic.

Previous arguments invoke the Galois action of \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong \mathbb{Z}/4 to track S_5-equivariance on Bring's surface coordinates. When this action restricts to the real values \varphi and 1/\varphi, the relevant group is the order-2 quotient \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})/\mathbb{Q}). Here, \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5}) \subset \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{10}) is the maximal real subfield.

The quartet orbit simplifies these arguments by eliminating \zeta_5. Rather than fixing \varphi as a real combination under the \zeta_5-action, identify the golden quartet Q as closed under the G-action, with \varphi serving as an orbit representative. This avoids unnecessary roots-of-unity bookkeeping.

Connection to Bring's surface.

The quartic P(x) = x^4 - 3x^2 + 1 is the maximal real subfield shadow of the resolvent determining the chiral fibration of Bring's surface. Evaluating the depressed-quartic formula 16d(b^2 - 4d)^2 at b = -3, d = 1 gives the discriminant \mathrm{disc}(P) = 400 = 2^4 \cdot 5^2. This value encodes the depth of the \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})/\mathbb{Q})-extension supporting the S_5 symmetry restricted to A_4 \subset S_5.

The four golden values form the complete real Galois orbit generated by \varphi (or 1/\varphi) and the bar involution. They encode the full set of phase boundaries and Möbius fixed points of the Descartes universe.

prop:moduli-symmetry-d4:
Proposition Dihedral D_4-action on the moduli line \mathbb{C}^\times generated by \sigma\colon q \mapsto iq and \tau\colon q \mapsto q^{-1}; golden octet as D_4-orbit. The two natural involutions on the aether moduli line \mathbb{C}^\times,

  \sigma\colon q \mapsto iq
  \qquad\text{(complex rotation by \(\pi/2\))},
  \qquad
  \tau\colon q \mapsto q^{-1}
  \qquad\text{(Hecke bar involution)},

generate a faithful action of the dihedral group of order 8:

  D_4
   =  \langle\,\sigma,\,\tau \;\mid\; \sigma^4 = \tau^2 = (\sigma\tau)^2 = 1\,\rangle.

The relation (\sigma\tau)^2 = 1 enforces the dihedral commutation \tau\sigma\tau = \sigma^{-1}. Verification:

  \tau\sigma\tau(q)
   =  \tau(\sigma(q^{-1}))
   =  \tau(iq^{-1})
   =  (iq^{-1})^{-1}
   =  -iq
   =  \sigma^{-1}(q).

The golden octet.

The D_4-orbit of \varphi in \mathbb{C}^\times forms the golden octet:

  G_8
   :=  D_4 \cdot \varphi
   =  \bigl\{\,\varphi,\;i\varphi,\;-\varphi,\;-i\varphi,\;
              1/\varphi,\;i/\varphi,\;-1/\varphi,\;-i/\varphi\,\bigr\}.

The eight elements partition by stabilizer into two cosets:

Coset Elements Generator Real / imaginary
\sigma\langle 1\rangle-orbit through \varphi \{\varphi, i\varphi, -\varphi, -i\varphi\} \sigma^k \cdot \varphi real (golden quartet Q_+) plus imaginary axis
\sigma\langle 1\rangle-orbit through 1/\varphi \{1/\varphi, i/\varphi, -1/\varphi, -i/\varphi\} \sigma^k \cdot 1/\varphi bar-image of Q_+, by \tau

The intersection G_8 \cap \mathbb{R} recovers the golden quartet Q = \{\,\varphi,\,-\varphi,\,1/\varphi,\,-1/\varphi\,\} (golden-quartet-galois). The intersection G_8 \cap i\mathbb{R} recovers its \pi/2-rotation iQ = \{\,i\varphi,\,-i\varphi,\,i/\varphi,\,-i/\varphi\,\}.

Equivalently, the octet contains the eight roots of

  P_{\mathbb{C}}(z)  :=  P(z) \cdot P(z/i)
   =  (z^4 - 3z^2 + 1)(z^4 + 3z^2 + 1)
   =  z^8 - 7z^4 + 1

over \mathbb{Q}(i), where P(z) = z^4 - 3z^2 + 1 is the quartic of the golden quartet.
